topicName: The Family and Social Relations in Islam
description: An overview of the importance of the family in Islam, the rights and responsibilities of family members, kinship and neighbourly ties, good manners, brotherhood and the building of a peaceful, just Muslim society.

mcq.questionText: Which Arabic term refers to dutifulness and kindness to one's parents?
mcq.explanation: Birr al-walidayn means goodness and obedience towards parents, a duty that the Qur'an places immediately after the worship of Allah.

mcq.questionText: In Islam, the family is regarded as:

options.text: An optional arrangement with no religious value
The basic unit and foundation of a healthy society
A burden that distracts from worship

mcq.explanation: Islam treats the family as the cornerstone of society; strong, righteous families produce a strong, moral community (ummah).

mcq.questionText: Maintaining good relations with relatives is known in Arabic as:
mcq.explanation: Silat al-rahim means joining the ties of kinship; cutting off relatives is strongly condemned in Islam.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the duty of a husband towards his wife?

options.text: To provide maintenance and treat her with kindness and justice
To prevent her from learning her religion
To deny her any share of inheritance

mcq.explanation: The husband is responsible for the maintenance (nafaqah) of his wife and must live with her honourably, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught that the best of people are the best to their families.

mcq.questionText: The upbringing and moral training of children in Islam is called:
mcq.explanation: Tarbiyah is the nurturing and education of children in faith, morals and good conduct, a key responsibility of parents.

mcq.questionText: Brotherhood among Muslims is referred to as:
mcq.explanation: Ukhuwah is the bond of Islamic brotherhood; the Qur'an states that the believers are but brothers.

mcq.questionText: Concerning neighbours, the Prophet (peace be upon him) emphasised their rights so often that the Companions thought:

options.text: Neighbours might be given a share of inheritance
Neighbours had no rights at all
One should never speak to a neighbour

mcq.explanation: The Prophet repeatedly stressed the rights of the neighbour until the Companions thought a neighbour might even inherit; this shows the high status of neighbourly rights.

mcq.questionText: Which quality means treating people fairly and giving everyone their due rights?
mcq.explanation: Adl is justice; Islam commands believers to be just even against their own interests, building a fair society.

mcq.questionText: The collective body of all Muslims worldwide is called the:
mcq.explanation: The ummah is the global community of Muslims united by faith, likened by the Prophet to one body that feels pain together.

mcq.questionText: How should a child treat parents who have grown old, according to the Qur'an?

options.text: By saying 'uff' (a word of contempt) to them
By abandoning them in their old age
By lowering the wing of humility, speaking gently and praying for them
By treating them only if they are wealthy

mcq.explanation: The Qur'an forbids even saying 'uff' to parents and commands kindness, humility and the prayer, 'My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small.'

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a right of a wife over her husband?

options.text: Maintenance, kind treatment and the teaching of her religion
Being forbidden to keep her own property
Being prevented from visiting righteous relatives

mcq.explanation: A wife has the right to provision, honourable treatment and religious guidance; she also retains full ownership of her own wealth.

mcq.questionText: Islam's command to care for the orphan teaches that the guardian must:

options.text: Protect the orphan and safeguard his or her property

mcq.explanation: The Qur'an warns against devouring an orphan's wealth and the Prophet promised that the one who cares for an orphan will be close to him in Paradise.

mcq.questionText: Which statement best reflects the Islamic teaching on truthfulness (sidq)?

options.text: Lying is acceptable in all business dealings
Truthfulness leads to righteousness and to Paradise
A Muslim need not be honest with non-relatives

mcq.explanation: The Prophet taught that truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise, while lying leads to wickedness and the Fire.

options.text: Obeying just laws, paying dues and contributing to the public good
Refusing to help others in need

mcq.explanation: Islam encourages Muslims to be responsible citizens by upholding justice, fulfilling obligations and working for the welfare of the whole community.

mcq.questionText: The Prophet (peace be upon him) likened the believers in their mutual love and mercy to:

options.text: A single body; when one part suffers, the whole body responds
Strangers who owe each other nothing

mcq.explanation: This famous hadith describes the unity of the ummah, comparing it to one body that feels the pain of any of its parts, reflecting deep brotherhood and solidarity.

fib.questionText: The Arabic term for dutifulness and kindness to parents is _____.
fib.explanation: Birr al-walidayn is the obligation of treating parents with goodness, obedience and respect.

fib.questionText: Maintaining the bonds of kinship with relatives is called _____ in Arabic.
fib.explanation: Silat al-rahim means joining the ties of the womb (kinship), which Islam commands and rewards.

fib.questionText: The brotherhood that unites Muslims is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Ukhuwah refers to Islamic brotherhood, founded on shared faith rather than blood or tribe.

fib.questionText: The whole worldwide community of Muslims is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The ummah is the single nation of believers united by Islam.

fib.questionText: The financial maintenance a husband must provide for his wife and family is called _____.
fib.explanation: Nafaqah is the husband's obligation to provide food, clothing and shelter for his dependants.

fib.questionText: The upbringing and moral training of children is called _____.
fib.explanation: Tarbiyah is the nurturing of children in faith and good character, a duty of parents.

fib.questionText: Truthfulness, an essential Islamic virtue, is called _____ in Arabic.
fib.explanation: Sidq means truthfulness in speech and action and leads to righteousness.

fib.questionText: Justice, the giving of every person their due right, is called _____ in Arabic.
fib.explanation: Adl (justice) is a foundation of a peaceful Islamic society and is commanded throughout the Qur'an.

fib.questionText: A child who has lost his or her father is called an _____ in Islam.
fib.explanation: Islam gives the orphan special rights to protection, care and the safeguarding of property.

fib.questionText: The Prophet said the best of you are those who are best to their _____.
fib.explanation: This hadith shows that good treatment of one's family is a measure of a person's character.

tf.questionText: The Qur'an places kindness to parents immediately after the command to worship Allah alone.
tf.explanation: Several verses join the command to worship Allah with the command to be good to one's parents, showing the high status of this duty.

tf.questionText: Cutting off the ties of kinship is praised and encouraged in Islam.
tf.explanation: Cutting off kinship (qati'at al-rahim) is strongly condemned; Islam commands joining the ties of relationship (silat al-rahim).

tf.questionText: A wife in Islam has the right to maintenance and kind treatment from her husband.
tf.explanation: Among a wife's rights are provision (nafaqah), honourable companionship and instruction in her religion.

tf.questionText: Islam teaches that neighbours, whether Muslim or non-Muslim, have rights upon us.
tf.explanation: The Prophet stressed the rights of the neighbour generally, and Islam includes both near and distant neighbours in this kindness.

tf.questionText: A guardian is permitted to wrongfully consume an orphan's wealth.
tf.explanation: The Qur'an severely warns those who unjustly devour the property of orphans, comparing it to swallowing fire into their bellies.

tf.questionText: Honouring the elderly is part of good manners (akhlaq) in Islam.
tf.explanation: The Prophet taught that the one who does not respect our elders and show mercy to our young is not from us.

tf.questionText: The believers are described in the Qur'an as enemies to one another.
tf.explanation: The Qur'an says, 'The believers are but brothers,' establishing brotherhood (ukhuwah), not enmity.

tf.questionText: Truthfulness leads to righteousness and ultimately to Paradise, according to the Prophet.
tf.explanation: The hadith states that truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise, while lying leads to the Fire.

tf.questionText: A Muslim has no responsibility towards the wider community in which he or she lives.
tf.explanation: Islam encourages cooperation in good, helping the needy, and being a responsible citizen who contributes to the welfare of society.

tf.questionText: Helping the poor and the needy through charity strengthens social bonds in the Muslim community.
tf.explanation: Charity such as zakah and sadaqah supports the poor, reduces inequality and builds compassion and unity within the ummah.

summary.questionText: Why is the family considered important in Islam?
summary.correctAnswer: The family is the basic unit and foundation of society in Islam. Strong, righteous families nurture good values, provide love, security and moral training, and produce upright members who build a healthy and stable community.
summary.explanation: Islam protects the family through clear rights and duties because a sound society begins with a sound home.

summary.questionText: State three rights of parents over their children.
summary.correctAnswer: Children must obey their parents in what is good, treat them with kindness and respect (birr al-walidayn), care for them especially in old age, speak to them gently, and pray for them.
summary.explanation: The Qur'an commands excellence to parents and forbids even a word of contempt towards them.

summary.questionText: Mention the rights of children over their parents.
summary.correctAnswer: Children have the right to be given a good name, to be loved and provided for, to be protected, and above all to receive proper upbringing (tarbiyah), education and training in faith and good character.
summary.explanation: Tarbiyah is a trust (amanah) from Allah; parents are responsible for guiding their children to righteousness.

summary.questionText: What are the mutual rights of the husband and wife in Islam?
summary.correctAnswer: The husband must provide maintenance, treat his wife kindly and justly, and guide her in religion. The wife should care for the home, protect her husband's honour and property, and cooperate with him. Both owe each other love, faithfulness, mercy and good companionship.
summary.explanation: Marriage in Islam is built on mutual rights, tranquillity (sakinah), love and mercy (mawaddah wa rahmah).

summary.questionText: Explain the meaning and importance of silat al-rahim.
summary.correctAnswer: Silat al-rahim means maintaining the ties of kinship by visiting relatives, helping them, showing kindness and keeping in contact. It is highly rewarded, said to increase one's provision and lengthen one's life, while cutting off kinship is a major sin.
summary.explanation: Keeping kinship ties strengthens the extended family and the wider social fabric.

summary.questionText: Describe the rights of neighbours in Islam.
summary.correctAnswer: Neighbours have the right to be treated with kindness, to be greeted, helped in need, not harmed by word or deed, to have their privacy respected, and to be shared with, for example by giving them food. These rights apply to both Muslim and non-Muslim neighbours.
summary.explanation: The Prophet so stressed neighbours' rights that the Companions thought a neighbour might inherit.

summary.questionText: How does Islam command the care of the orphan, the poor and the needy?
summary.correctAnswer: Islam commands believers to protect orphans, safeguard their wealth and bring them up well, and to support the poor and needy through zakah, sadaqah and kindness. Caring for orphans and the destitute is a sign of true faith and a means of nearness to Allah.
summary.explanation: These commands reduce poverty and inequality and build a compassionate, just society.

summary.questionText: List the good manners (akhlaq) that Islam encourages in society.
summary.correctAnswer: Islam encourages truthfulness (sidq), justice (adl), kindness, cooperation in good (ta'awun), respect for others, honesty, keeping promises, modesty (haya), patience and forgiveness, while forbidding lying, injustice, backbiting, arrogance and harming others.
summary.explanation: Good akhlaq is at the heart of the Prophet's mission, who said he was sent to perfect noble character.

summary.questionText: Explain the concept of ukhuwah and the unity of the ummah.
summary.correctAnswer: Ukhuwah is the brotherhood of all Muslims based on shared faith. The ummah is the single worldwide community of believers, likened by the Prophet to one body in which, if one part suffers, the whole responds. This unity calls for mutual love, support, cooperation and the avoidance of division.
summary.explanation: Brotherhood and unity overcome tribalism and racism, binding believers as equals before Allah.

summary.questionText: How does Islam help to build a peaceful and just society?
summary.correctAnswer: Islam builds peace and justice by establishing the rights and duties of every person, commanding justice and honesty, forbidding oppression and corruption, caring for the weak, encouraging cooperation and charity, promoting good citizenship, and uniting people through brotherhood and shared moral values.
summary.explanation: When rights are honoured and good character prevails, society becomes secure, fair and harmonious.

hoq.questionText: A young Muslim works far from home and rarely contacts his aging parents and relatives, claiming he is too busy. Which Islamic teaching most directly corrects this behaviour?

options.text: Birr al-walidayn and silat al-rahim require him to honour his parents and maintain kinship ties despite his work
He is free of any duty once he is financially independent
Work always outweighs family obligations in Islam
Kindness to parents ends when a child becomes an adult

hoq.explanation: Kindness to parents (birr al-walidayn) and keeping kinship ties (silat al-rahim) remain obligatory throughout life; he should stay in contact, support and care for them even while working.

hoq.questionText: Two Muslim neighbours from different tribes quarrel and stop speaking, while members of the mosque take sides along tribal lines. Which combination of Islamic principles best resolves this situation?

options.text: Ukhuwah, justice and the rights of the neighbour, which unite believers beyond tribe and call for reconciliation
Ignoring the dispute since neighbours have no rights
Allowing division because unity of the ummah is optional

hoq.explanation: Islamic brotherhood (ukhuwah) transcends tribe, justice (adl) demands fairness, and neighbours have strong rights; together these call for reconciliation and the rejection of tribal partisanship that divides the ummah.

hoq.questionText: A wealthy guardian manages an orphan's inheritance and is tempted to use it for his own needs, while neglecting the orphan's schooling. Evaluating this through Islamic teaching, what should he do?

options.text: Spend the orphan's wealth freely since he is the guardian
Safeguard the orphan's property, refrain from consuming it unjustly, and ensure the orphan's upbringing and education
Delay the orphan's care until the child is an adult
Treat the orphan harshly to discourage dependence

hoq.explanation: The Qur'an forbids devouring an orphan's wealth and commands its protection; a guardian must act with trust (amanah), preserve the property and provide proper care and education, for the Prophet praised those who look after orphans.
